name: Multi-view Equivariant Stability Persistence
scientific_question: A real defect, observed under mild lighting/flip/small geometric transforms and transformed back to the original coordinates, should persist; spurious hotspots from interpolation, local texture or a single lucky feature match are typically unstable. Can cross-view equivariant consistency (same frozen A1/AnomalyDINO pipeline per view, no second model) raise the anomaly map?

view_set.rules: only pre-registered invertible/alignable transforms; rotated-view effective area excludes border via mask; NO random crops that can remove the defect; NO per-category hand-picked transforms

phase_r0_geometry_audit.images: 10 MPDD normal reference images (pre-registered deterministic list)
phase_r0_geometry_audit.measures: inverse-transform geometric error (corner/landmark RMSE) per view; confirm stability is not manufactured by interpolation
phase_r0_geometry_audit.baseline_duplicate_control: monotone-copy of base map as fake multi-view must NOT pass the persistence contrast
phase_r0_geometry_audit.cost: per-image added inference time and peak VRAM for the full 6-view set on RTX 3060

r0_candidates.B1_median: score map = median over views of inverse-transformed A1 maps
r0_candidates.B2_stability: base * (0.75 + 0.25 * stability), stability = 1 - normalized MAD over views (suppress unstable hotspots only)
r0_candidates.B3_persistence: keep original score for A1 connected regions persisting in >= 4/5 views at pre-registered quantile thresholds, else x0.8

gates_r0.g1: geometry audit: inverse error small enough that transform chain is faithful on normals
gates_r0.g2: mean Pixel-AP gain >= +0.005 over A1 across shots 1/2/4; 3/3 shots positive; >= 4/6 categories positive; worst category >= -0.015
gates_r0.g4: true multi-view beats misaligned-view control by >= +0.002
gates_r0.cost_note: if inference > 5x A1, try B-lite (original + flip + one brightness) and report separately

leakage: all transforms pre-registered and identical across categories; no GT in score path
